content.text:
I submitted the portfolio. It got a training Sharpe of 0.36 and **failed** the sealed 2000–2012 validation check. That was the only backtest I ran, out of the 200 allowed.

I stopped after one test on purpose. In the 1970–1999 data, a signal's Sharpe in one period says almost nothing about the next: the correlation between periods was about 0.0. So a search that keeps trying portfolios until one passes would mostly be finding luck in the validation data, and the PASS would no longer mean the portfolio works.

**Final portfolio:** an equal-weighted basket of all 47 `hold_<IND>` signals blended 50/50 with an equal-weighted basket of all 47 `ma_<IND>_21_63` trend signals, each basket scaled so it contributes the same risk. I picked it using only training data, because it was the simplest family-level combination with a positive Sharpe in all five 6-year training periods (0.26–0.64).
